findings.issue: Root ErrorBoundary renders 'Not found' for every error, including 500s from the API (thrown ApiError) and unexpected exceptions; real outages look like missing pages and no error details are ever shown.
findings.suggestion: Follow the documented pattern: accept Route.ErrorBoundaryProps (or useRouteError), branch on isRouteErrorResponse vs Error vs unknown, and render distinct 500/404 UIs.

findings.issue: Not-found is handled with a per-route 'notFound: true as const' sentinel plus 'notFound' in loaderData checks in every component and meta, duplicated across pokemon/move/ability/type/routes.tsx:1-10 routes, instead of the documented throw data("Not Found", {status:404}) + route ErrorBoundary flow.
findings.suggestion: Throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 }) from loaders and render a shared NotFound in each route's ErrorBoundary (or centralise the sentinel handling), removing the boilerplate from five files.

findings.issue: Artwork falls back to a fabricated spritePatternUrl when the API returns null for official-artwork, which can produce a broken for sets the API explicitly doesn't ship.
findings.suggestion: Render nothing (or a placeholder) when the API URL is null; the spec says null means missing.

findings.issue: Search text lives in useState seeded from the URL once; after typing (replace) then paging (push), browser back/forward can restore an older q in the URL while the input and filters keep the newer local value.
findings.suggestion: Sync local q from searchParams via useEffect on popstate, or drive q entirely from useSearchParams.

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent(params.name) re-decodes params React Router already decoded; a URL containing a lone '%' throws URIError (and name normalization should not depend on decoding).
findings.suggestion: Use params.name as-is and just lowercase it (same in move.tsx:8, ability.tsx:8, type.tsx:18).

findings.issue: apiGet has no timeout/AbortController, so a hung upstream request stalls the SSR response indefinitely with no retry path for that request.
findings.suggestion: Add an AbortSignal.timeout (e.g. 5-10s) to fetch and surface it as a 502-style error.

findings.issue: Damage-relations badges inline a copy of the TypeBadge markup (span.type-badge with the var(--type-<name>) style) instead of reusing the shared component.
findings.suggestion: Import and render TypeBadge from app/app/components/ui.tsx:28.

findings.issue: API responses are typed as 'any' throughout the data layer and loaders (apiGet<any> at :100,:140,:155; move.tsx:9-22; pokemon.tsx:45-61), discarding TypeScript's help in a repo that otherwise sets up generated route types.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal response interfaces (Species, Pokemon, Move, Type, Ability) in the data layer and have apiGet default to them.

findings.issue: spriteUrl exists twice with different signatures (server: (id) in pokeapi.server.ts:71, client: (apiBase, id) here), and the num() em-dash helper is duplicated in move.tsx:25 and pokemon.tsx:254.
findings.suggestion: Have the server layer reuse the same base+id helper (or export one function taking the base), and hoist num into lib/format.ts.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic, current-stable React Router 8.5.1 framework-mode app: correct route modules, generated types, a well-bounded server-only data layer and clean client/server seams, with only light duplication and a pervasive use of 'any'. The two changes I'd require before merge are making the root ErrorBoundary distinguish 404s from real errors, and replacing the five-times-duplicated notFound sentinel with the framework's documented throw data()/ErrorBoundary flow. Everything else is nits — I'd merge it after one focused round.
